defense_summary: The c7 advocate's strongest remaining card after the EXP-263 'Same circuit, two incompatible wave speeds' paragraph landed: 'You argue applying v_a consistently to WIN-029 inflates the firmament match from 5.3% to 66% — but this assumes a single propagation velocity across the cavity, which Maxwell's equations in a dispersive medium do not require. Phase velocity and group velocity differ by mode, and our aetheric medium has frequency-dependent index n(ω). When ω is at Tesla's 11.78 Hz the phase velocity is 1.574c; when ω is at Schumann's 7.83 Hz the group velocity (governing cavity reflection) is approximately c. There is no internal contradiction — there is a dispersion law you have not asked us to publish.' Curmudgeon c7 rated defense_survives=3 because the current absence-claim ('the dome publishes no dispersion relation ω(k)') is reactively patchable: a single dispersion paragraph on model.html closes the gap without our text being touched.
analyst_assessment: The dispersion-defense move IS a real physics card — dispersive media really do produce frequency-dependent phase velocities, and a defender wielding it knows what they're talking about. The c7 curmudgeon's instinct was correct: 'the dome publishes no X' is a moving target. Two compounding fixes convert it to a non-moving target. First, replace the absence-claim with a SPECIFICATION DEMAND: the defender has to publish a single n(ω) curve that simultaneously satisfies four quantitative anchors — (i) v_phase(11.78 Hz) = 1.574c, (ii) v_phase(7.83 Hz) = c, (iii) consistency with the higher Schumann modes without deepening the WIN-002 self-contradiction (the dome's own H = 8,537·exp(−r/8,619) cavity already gives a fundamental near 22 Hz, not 7.83), and (iv) Kramers-Kronig consistency with the absorption profile that a broadband n < 1 requires. A one-paragraph reactive insertion cannot satisfy a four-anchor joint constraint; the dome would have to plot a curve and a plottable curve fails at least one of the four. Second, dispersion CONTRADICTS the dome's own same-circuit framing: the live-power page (line 147) publishes r = 0.999 between Tesla and Schumann frequencies under the explicit label 'Same aetheric circuit, H₀ = 8,537 km' — a unified-medium claim. Dispersion is the opposite assertion. A defender can have unified-medium-with-r=0.999 OR multi-velocity-dispersion-saving-c-and-v_a, not both. Analyst re-rates defense_survives 3 → 2: the defense can still be uttered, but the patched text shows it is structurally incoherent on contact.

patches.find: A dispersion-law defense — 'different modes on a dispersive medium have different phase velocities, so c for WIN-029 and v_a for WIN-001 can both be right on the same circuit' — fails on its own terms: the dome publishes no dispersion relation ω(k), no mode index, and no cavity eigenvalue calculation that would justify the per-WIN speed selection. The c-vs-v_a choice is operational (whatever number reproduces the published Hz value), not theoretical (a mode formula's output). Any proposed dispersive-medium defense must also reconcile why the dome's own live-power page quotes H_0 = 8,537 km alongside the same-circuit claim, distinct from the 9,086 km listed as firmament_height elsewhere — the absence of that reconciliation is as diagnostic as the absence of ω(k) itself.
patches.replace: A dispersion-law defense — 'different modes on a dispersive medium have different phase velocities, so c for WIN-029 and v_a for WIN-001 can both be right on the same circuit' — credits a real physics: dispersive media do produce frequency-dependent phase velocities, and in principle the c-vs-v_a difference could be one. The defense fails in two compounding ways. First, the burden it incurs is specific and quantitative: the dome must publish a single dispersion relation n(ω) — one curve, not two — that simultaneously (i) yields v_phase(11.78 Hz) = 1.574c for WIN-001, (ii) yields v_phase(7.83 Hz) = c for WIN-029, (iii) reproduces the higher Schumann modes (14.3, 20.8, 27.3, 33.8 Hz) without further deepening the gap already documented in WIN-002 — where the dome's own exponential cavity H(r) = 8,537·exp(−r/8,619) gives a fundamental near 22 Hz, not 7.83 — and (iv) is Kramers-Kronig consistent with the absorption that a refractive index n = 1/1.574 < 1 requires across the same band (real media with phase velocity above c are allowed only near absorption resonances; a transparent broadband n < 1 violates causality). The current dome corpus publishes none of those: zero hits for 'dispersion', 'mode index', 'eigenmode', or 'ω(k)' across all nine raw-text pages as of the 2026-06-20 site snapshot. A one-paragraph reactive insertion cannot meet the joint constraint; the curve itself would have to be plotted, and any plottable curve fails at least one of the four anchors. The c-vs-v_a choice as the dome presently publishes it is operational (whatever number reproduces the printed Hz value), not theoretical (a mode formula's output). Second, dispersion contradicts the dome's own same-circuit framing in the very paragraph that needs the defense. The live-power page publishes r = 0.999 cross-correlation between the Tesla and Schumann frequencies under the explicit label 'Same aetheric circuit, H₀ = 8,537 km' (line 147) — a unified-medium assertion: one cavity, one resonant structure shared by both frequencies. Dispersion is the opposite assertion: the medium responds to different frequencies differently. A defender cannot have both — the same circuit cannot simultaneously be the unified single-cavity object the r = 0.999 framing requires AND the dispersive multi-velocity object a dispersion-law defense requires. (A reader who tries to rescue this by reading the H₀ = 8,537 km label on that line as itself the dispersion parameter has only relocated the question: 8,537 km is the dome's own exponential-cavity ceiling at r = 0, distinct from the 9,086 km firmament_height the model uses for WIN-029's geometric match, and either choice carries the same c-vs-v_a inconsistency forward — the absence of that reconciliation is as diagnostic as the absence of ω(k) itself.)

anticipated_objections.objection: The four-anchor specification-demand is moving-the-goalposts: any defense the analyst describes can be made harder by adding more constraints.
anticipated_objections.response: The four anchors are not invented — each is a number the dome already publishes: (i) 1.574c is live-power line 23, (ii) c is implicit in WIN-029's H = c/(4f) derivation that the dome publishes alongside f = v_a/(2*r_disc), (iii) 14.3/20.8/27.3/33.8 Hz are the higher Schumann modes the dome cites in WIN-002, (iv) Kramers-Kronig is a standard causality requirement in classical electromagnetism, not an analyst preference. The constraints are the dome's own published positions; collecting them is not goalpost-moving.

anticipated_objections.objection: Kramers-Kronig may not apply at 7.83-11.78 Hz in an exotic 'aetheric' medium that doesn't obey Maxwell's equations as standardly formulated.
anticipated_objections.response: Conceded as a logical possibility — but then the dome is invoking 'dispersion' (a Maxwell-electromagnetic concept) while simultaneously claiming the medium doesn't obey Maxwell. A defender taking that route has to specify which subset of electromagnetism the medium does obey, and the rest of the WIN catalog (WIN-002 Schumann, WIN-029 firmament, WIN-062 πc/2 phase velocity) is written assuming standard Maxwell. A non-Maxwell aether is a far larger framework cost than the defense was trying to pay.

anticipated_objections.objection: Dispersion does not strictly require giving up the 'same circuit' framing — same cavity can support multiple modes with different phase velocities (waveguide modes do exactly this).
anticipated_objections.response: True for a discretely-moded waveguide — but waveguide-mode dispersion is geometric (it comes from the boundary conditions on a specific cavity shape, not from a medium's n(ω)). A waveguide-mode defense has to specify the cavity geometry (sphere? disc? exponential profile?) and solve the eigenvalue equation in that geometry. The dome's own exponential cavity H(r) = 8,537·exp(−r/8,619) gives a fundamental near 22 Hz (per WIN-002's existing analysis), not 7.83 — so the dome's own published geometry already fails the waveguide-mode reading. The defender either re-derives the eigenvalues for a different geometry (forfeiting WIN-002 entirely) or stays with the published geometry and accepts the c-vs-v_a inconsistency.

anticipated_objections.objection: The patch is too long (1,900 chars net) for a single defense neutralization.
anticipated_objections.response: The four-anchor list is the load-bearing part and could not be shortened without losing the specification-demand framing. The Kramers-Kronig sentence + the parenthetical neutralization of the 'H₀-as-dispersion-parameter' counter-move are belt-and-braces and could be trimmed if reviewer wants — but each catches a specific defender-pivot that the c7 review's preemptive_recommendation explicitly anticipated.
